subject: K-fold cross-validation/Future predictions for hierarchical models

messages.author: d8614c9819918597
messages.subject: K-fold cross-validation/Future predictions for hierarchical models
parts:
Hello Stan Users,

This may be a stupid question but I am a bit confused. In K-fold cross-validation and/or future predictions, how do you deal with random effects in hierarchical models given that, they are individual specific? In short, if I have a held-out set do I have to estimate the random effects for this set or use the ones estimated in the training set? And if I have to, how do I go about it?

For instance, I have a model with 4 random effects estimated as:

b~multi_normal_cholesky(mu_b, L_Sigma_b); with priors on mu_b and L_Sigma_b.  Should I do the same for the held-out set?

Thank you for your kind response.

 

Olive

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] K-fold cross-validation/Future predictions for hierarchical models
parts:
This gets to a subtlety in predictive comparisons in hierarchical models.  There are
two interpretations of prediction — either you can sample new data conditioned on the
same groups, or you can sample new groups from the hierarchical population distribution
and then new data from those groups.  Ultimately this is related to whether the random
effects are considered part of the prior (in which case predictions use set the random
effects to their inferred values) or part of the likelihood as missing data (in which case
predictions sample new random effects and then data conditioned on those).  

If your random effects are individual specific then you’ll have to sample new random
effects from the hierarchical population distribution and then new data from those
random effects.  This will give you a predictive distribution that you can compare to
any new data.
